description: Standard 200 litre steel drum stood upright with rolling ribs and a dented rim

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Standard 200 litre steel drum stood upright with rolling ribs and a dented rim Materials: heavily rusted blue paint, peeling, oil streaks down the side.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: Optimization-pass: nothing to optimise, because the budget was designed to in the blockout rather than optimised into at the end. Final measurement off the BUILT scene: 1864 triangles / 2000, 2 draw calls / 2, 2 materials / 2, 2 unique geometries / 2 -- at ceiling on three axes and 93 percent of the fourth. The two-component split IS the design, so there is nothing left to merge and no pivot hung off a part that would have had to be merged. No decimation: 44 radial segments at the 0.29 m hoop radius give 0.74 mm of chord error, 0.75 px on a 1024 px review render, so the tessellation tier was chosen up front and the authored profile points stay exact. VRAM is 22.4 MB across 4 canvas textures, halved from 44.7 MB by declaring the bung material textureless -- the generator had been building a second full 1024-square map set for a 64 mm part. Every gate re-run clean: turntable covered and unholed on all four azimuths, Tier 1 IoU 0.9152 / aspect 0.0027 / scale 0.0127 / per-part colour delta-E 16.27, attachment 0 unmeasured, part coverage 2 named parts and 0 unnamed. Honest shortfall recorded on rust-distribution: the plate carries more oxide and more contrast than the procedural field produces. Placement is right; amount is light.

featureReviews.notes: Held through the pass. No decimation was needed: 44 radial segments were chosen to the budget up front, so the measured profile points stay exact instead of being moved by a quadric collapse. IoU 0.9152, aspect delta 0.0027.
Held. Chimes at 0.2870 against the body's 0.2780, base chime the sole ground contact at y = 0.

Held, and scored honestly below the earlier 0.86 on the side-by-side. Distribution and direction are right -- oxide on both chimes, streaks falling, worn hoop crowns -- but the plate carries noticeably MORE oxide and more contrast: it has large rust blooms mid-panel and heavy multi-streak runs at the lower right that the procedural field does not reach. Above its 0.80 threshold, and the shortfall is amount, not placement.
Held. Closed at both ends, head recessed, no pinwheel.
Held. Four turntable azimuths, no two reflections of each other.

name: Oil Drum
notes: Sealed one-piece steel drum: not breakable and nothing unscrews, so it ships one root pivot at base-center, no sockets and no destruction groups. Declared height moved 0.88 -> 0.81 m on 2026-08-24: the reference plate draws the drum ~8% squatter than a real ISO 200 L drum, corroborated independently by the Meshy proxy (7.2%), and the build follows the plate so the model is scored against a reference it can match. Diameter 0.58 m is unchanged and is agreed by both sources.
